title: Filipinas Life Assurance Company v. Pedroso
summary: The Supreme Court ruled on the liability of an insurance company for the unauthorized acts of its agent. The insurer is liable when the agent's acts are within the apparent scope of authority and the insured relied on such authority in good faith.
doctrine: An insurance company is bound by the acts of its agents within the apparent scope of their authority. The doctrine of apparent authority or estoppel prevents the insurer from denying the authority of its agent when the insured relied on such authority in good faith.
fullText:
TINGA, J.:

The issue is whether Filipinas Life Assurance Company is liable for the unauthorized investment scheme of its agent.

The relationship between an insurance company and its agents is governed by the principles of agency. An agent can bind the principal only within the scope of actual or apparent authority.

The doctrine of apparent authority provides that where an insurance company, by its acts and conduct, holds out a person as an agent with authority to transact business, the company is bound by the acts of such person within the scope of apparent authority, even if the agent exceeded actual authority.
